text:
Maya: Heads-up — saw a KV cache memory growth regression on canary after the prefetch-window change (merged yesterday).
Devon: ugh, which change exactly? PR?
Maya: PR 4821 — increased prefetch_window from 16 -> 64 to boost long-context reuse. Metrics look good for throughput but resident mem climbs steadily on hosted canaries.
Priya: can you paste the kv stats dump?
Maya: here: `rundump --kv-stats --since 6h` output snippet:
```
KV_CACHE_RESIDENT_BYTES: 24.1GB -> 40.3GB
KV_PAGE_FAULTS: 12k -> 36k
KV_EVICTION_COUNT: 3.2k -> 12.8k
PREFETCH_WINDOW: 64
SLOT_FRAG_RATIO: 0.38
SLOTS_IN_USE: 1.9M -> 3.4M
```
Luca: frag ratio 0.38 is high — looks like we packed a lot of partial frames. Increasing prefetch may be allocating many small page-backed frames and never coalescing.
Devon: does this reproduce on Dedicated/private?
Maya: Dedicated canaries show milder growth: 24->30GB. Private on-prem (A100) showed almost no growth over 6h.
Priya: differences expected: hosted has MTU/Azure overlay + older linux kernel in the node image. Dedicated uses our tuned kernel + hugepage config. On-prem has NVLINK + different jemalloc knobs.
Luca: kernel selection matters: on hosted we fall back to generic mmap-backed allocation path because MAP_POPULATE isn't honored under our overlay. That increases page-churn.
Devon: any batching or kernel-selection logs?
Maya: added a short trace from the runtime: `kernel_choice: (attention): neon_opt -> fallback_generic_gemm` and `alloc_path: mmap_backed` around the spike.
Priya: that explains it — fallback GEMM path holds larger temporary KV frames for some layers and our prefetch forces them to be resident longer. On Dedicated, opt kernels produce smaller working set.
Luca: also check slab warmup: we observed slow coalesce in jemalloc when many small allocations come from prefetch. If slabs don't compact, fragmentation goes up.
Devon: can we repro with a smaller prefetch window? e.g., 32 or 8?
Maya: quick A/B: window=32 reduced resident to 33GB on hosted canary, window=16 (baseline) stays ~25GB. So it's non-linear.
Priya: looks like threshold behavior: above ~24 contiguous frames we trigger a different allocator path.
Luca: what about batching heuristics? Bigger prefetch + larger batch size could amplify because more KV pages are kept per request. Any observed latency regressions?
Maya: tail latency up ~4% at p99 for the canary with prefetch=64, throughput +6%. So tradeoff but memory growth unacceptable.
Devon: Ops-bot, can we revert the canary change for hosted-only and keep Dedicated canary running with prefetch=64?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Revert rollout queued. Canary group: hosted nodes targeted. ETA 3m. :gear:
Priya: meanwhile, we should add a telemetry flag: record alloc_path and slab_fragmentation metric per model so we can correlate quickly.
Luca: agree. Also add a kernel-selection whitelist — prefer optimized kernels for layers that touch KV heavily. We can gate prefetch expansion until kernel path is verified.
Maya: opening issue: infra/kv/1289 — notes + dumps + repro script. I'll attach short reproducer that runs a 12h longctx workload with prefetch toggle.
Devon: assign to runtime and infra, prioritize P0 for hosted regression.
Priya: long term: add automatic prefetch auto-tuner that backs off when fragmentation > 0.25 or evict rate grows >2x.
Luca: good. Also add a short doc for on-prem ops: jemalloc and hugepage knobs that help collate slabs (link later).
Maya: thanks — ops-bot confirmed revert. I'll post results after 1h. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Revert applied to hosted canaries at 3567000150. Canary health: green.
